Welcome to the eGo style battery recommendation thread. What is an eGo style battery? They're the ones that look like cigars. Like these bad boys.

A quick run-down on eGo batteries:

  • There are fixed voltage and variable voltage varieties. In short, the higher your voltage, the higher your output. Watch out, because if you turn it up too much, you can burn out your coils early.

  • Generally, the larger size the battery (or mAh rating [milliamp hour {don't say "MAH", also tacky}]), the more battery life.

  • Some of them let you charge while using them, these have a "passthrough mode".

  • Always buy in pairs so you can have a backup.

  • If you can handle a slightly larger device, you will get a lot more battery life and way more capabilities.

I have a Kanger Twist 1300 mAh battery. This was my first foray into variable anything, and I already had the EVOD 2 tank, so I figured why not? Well, for a VV battery, it's great. It lasts me about 2.5 days with regular use, and I can run it at about 4.0V with the 1.5 ohm coils with everything from 50/50 to 70/30 juice without burning.

I picked it up at a local vape shop for $35, if I recall. My biggest issue with it is that the voltage markings have gotten scraped off by carrying it in my pocket consistently. Other than that, it's great.

However, I'd honestly say save your money and go variable wattage if at all possible.
